theme: Raw and cinematic, forty minutes out

linkedin.text:
The landscapes that photograph like a film set are usually eleven hours away and cost accordingly. Sometimes they are forty minutes outside a city with direct flights.

This is the valley country south of Marrakesh, on a programme we produced. Red rock, dry riverbeds, and the kind of light that makes an ordinary group photo look like it was art-directed.

This matters more than it used to. A trip now generates hundreds of images that circulate internally for months — on Slack, in the year-end deck, in recruitment material. A landscape that flatters those photos does real work for you long after the group has flown home, and it costs nothing extra to choose one.

The practical note: this terrain has almost no shade and no infrastructure. Everything — water, seating, shade, toilets, power — arrives on a truck and leaves on a truck. Budget for that honestly or the day is uncomfortable in a way nobody forgets either.

Want a location that keeps paying you back in images? Send us your dates.
